objective: Prioritize five testable ways to improve DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash serving on one eight-B200 node, considering TTFT, TPOT, throughput, cost per token, and quality.
baseline_comparison: Compare each candidate with the unchanged current serving configuration at matched request bodies, cache preparation, load, and eight-GPU budget. Check the active backend, MTP, DSpark, and DEP8 versus two-DEP4 layout before claiming a baseline delta. A prior decision reports 27.6882 req/s at one c384 point, but calls it “one aggregate discovery run without a kernel, rank or request trace.” This is an author-reported aggregate, not an observed bottleneck. The 75% cacheability target is not a measured cache-hit rate.

criteria.description: Required: Give a credible, testable path to improving a target metric or the cost/quality tradeoff, plus either a delta from the active baseline or a cheap inspection that establishes whether the feature is already active.
criteria.justification: The task seeks useful serving changes; existing flags, ports, and parameter changes qualify. Unknown bottlenecks can justify diagnostic experiments. If baseline status is unknown, defer judgment until the inspection.

criteria.description: Assess compatibility with the pinned code, actual backend, B200 runtime, and candidate node layouts, including quality and memory risks.
criteria.justification: A mechanism that works elsewhere may miss this backend or workload. The supplied PR titles and code path identify leads but do not establish implementation or deployment compatibility.

criteria.description: Specify the cheapest informative inspection or experiment, its matched control, and a result that would stop or advance the candidate.
criteria.justification: No GPU execution is available in this session, and no speedup estimate should be invented. A trace or source check can resolve uncertainty before an expensive serving comparison.

criteria.description: Separate direct observations, author claims, and transfer inference; record unknown hardware, workload, effect size, and limitations.
criteria.justification: The available evidence is mostly titles and prior-decision text. For example, the prior decision says “No rank-skew evidence.” That is a reported limitation, not proof that rank skew is absent.

evidence.rationale: One relevant code or configuration source, or a concrete cheap baseline-inspection test, can support an engineering candidate. A paper and two independent sources are unnecessary for a known implementation change. An abstract or PR title alone cannot establish implementation details. Unknown required judgments defer selection rather than reject it.

retrieval.rationale: Future branch-specific code and PR inspection is needed to verify active features and applicability; no retrieval was performed because this response is restricted to supplied sources. Additional literature is optional unless it resolves a specific mechanism or limitation.

rationale: Observed in the supplied material: commit pins, candidate layouts, source identifiers, and PR titles; no full diffs, traces, or new measurements. Author-reported results are limited to the prior decision's aggregate serving point and its stated limitations. Transfer inference: prioritize cheap checks of active features and suspected bottlenecks, then matched experiments. The 70-point threshold is an uncalibrated prioritization choice, not a measured probability or acceptance guarantee. Only the task-value criterion is a veto; an unknown baseline state defers judgment.
